transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?

It is unlikely that the whole vacuum is necessarily dead. A red flashing light when the trigger is pressed usually means a protection fault rather than a confirmed motor failure; the main possibilities are a failing battery, a charging/contacts problem, or an airflow blockage making the battery protection cut in. First, check the charger is firmly in a known-working socket and seated properly, and wipe the charging contacts clean and dry. Then, with the vacuum switched off, remove the wand and floorhead and check the bin inlet and airway for a blockage. If it still gives the red flash after a proper charge with the airway clear, the battery becomes the most likely replaceable cause; an engineer or Dyson support would then be sensible before assuming the main machine has failed.

Tried the hallway socket as well and the charger light is on, but same result. The contacts look clean and there are no blockages: filter washed last month, bin empty. The battery isn't swollen, hot or smelly either. Is it the battery then?

Yes — the battery pack is now the leading suspect, but not proven yet. A charger’s own light only shows it has mains power; it does not confirm the charger is supplying the correct output or that the battery is accepting charge. Clean contacts and no heat/swelling, a battery protection or internal cell fault is more likely than the whole machine being dead; a trigger/control fault is less likely. Please check the light behaviour while the charger is connected, and count any red flashes on a trigger press if you can — that is the best way to separate a failed battery from charger or machine electronics. Do not keep repeatedly pulling the trigger if the battery becomes warm, smells unusual or swells; disconnect the charger and stop using it.

While it's on the charger the blue lights come on, then it sometimes shows the flashing red too. When I press the trigger it's a single red light flashing about once a second, no blue ones. Is that enough to say it's the battery?

[Heading: Likely cause: battery — flat or failed (cordless)]
It is enough to make the battery the most likely fault, but not enough to prove it absolutely. A V10 that will not start, shows no blue run lights and flashes red even while connected to charge is behaving more like a battery pack whose internal protection has tripped or whose cells have failed than a blockage issue. The remaining alternative is the charger: its indicator and the vacuum’s blue charge lights show activity, but do not prove it is charging correctly; a main-machine fault is less likely. I would not assume the whole vacuum is dead. Use Dyson’s official spares/support route or a reputable vacuum repairer to confirm with a known-good compatible charger or battery before buying one. Do not use a damaged, swollen, hot or non-approved battery pack; if the red flashing continues on charge, unplug it and leave it disconnected.
